author: reek
body: The Driver is read-only across the chapters it cites -- it composes their existing operations rather than reaching into their internals.

author: reek
body: driver-init builds an empty driver around a freshly-generated keypair. open-file refreshes the source index for the file the editor just loaded; the chapter name is parsed off the file path.

author: reek
body: The Reader-side calls combine H1's lookup with H3's trust filter. annotations-here returns what the bubble should display for the current cursor.

author: reek
body: annotate-cursor is the H2 entry point. The caller supplies kind, body, and timestamp; the driver looks up the def under cursor, signs and stores via author-annotation-at, and folds the resulting AnnotationFact back into its state. Returns the new driver plus the SignedAnnotation (so the caller can pass it to publish-cursor if they want to publish too).

author: reek
body: inject-incoming is the TrustService adapter's entry point. It records the proposal in the local AnnotationStore (so the reader sees it) and appends to the editor's notification queue (so the user sees a throbber/toast).

author: reek
body: inject-verdict is the inbound side for the original annotator -- a verdict on a proposal we authored. The H10 EditorVerdicts inbox filters by authored-proposals, so the editor only learns of verdicts on its own proposals.

author: reek
body: The transport adapter calls drain-* to pull pending payloads, sends them, and then asks the driver to clear what was drained. The two outboxes (proposals and verdicts) drain independently.

author: reek
body: driver-pump-out drains both outboxes onto a TrustSession in one call, returning the new driver state, the post-send session, and a count. driver-receive is the inverse -- given an AgentMessage lifted off the session, it routes annotations through the trust filter into the repo and the editor notifications, and routes verdicts through inject-verdict so the originating editor's EditorVerdicts inbox sees them too.
